orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
orders.reason: annual screening resumed after treated TB

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Weight back to 84 kg. Dialysis steady, rides mostly reliable. A1c in September was 7.9; sugar log since then fasting 110s-180s. Two readings in the 70s late morning, felt fine, ate. No lows needing help.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Lungs clear. No edema. AVF thrill/bruit. Feet intact.

A/P
T2DM - A1c today; no change.
HTN - at his usual on lisinopril 5.
Lung screening - resume annual LDCT; radiology to compare with the 2021 film.
RTC 4 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, compared with February 2019 and the May 2021 chest radiograph. New since 2019: linear scarring at the right apex, consistent with prior granulomatous infection in this patient with treated tuberculosis. No solid or part-solid nodules. No consolidation or cavitation. No adenopathy. Coronary calcification, mild.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2, benign appearance. Right apical post-inflammatory scarring. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT lung screening
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Lung-RADS 2. Right apical scarring from treated TB; no nodule of concern. Annual follow-up.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening CT shows some scar at the top of the right lung where the TB was - that's expected and harmless. No spots that worry us. Next one in a year. Your A1c from January was 7.6, a little better.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED - physician record, visit 05/07/2022 (faxed on request).

CC: lightheaded with heart racing while out walking this morning.
HPI: 70 y/o man, ESRD on HD MWF, T2DM on basal-bolus insulin, anemia, remote TB (treated). For about two weeks has had spells of dizziness and a pounding heartbeat during his morning walk, happening more often. Today's episode was worse and a neighbor drove him in. Took glargine last night as usual and lispro with a small breakfast.
Meds per patient: insulin glargine, insulin lispro sliding scale, metformin, lisinopril, sevelamer, aspirin, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 40 pk-yr. No alcohol. Retired postal worker.

Triage: BP 130/80, HR 98. Diaphoretic, anxious, alert and oriented.
POC glucose at arrival during symptoms: 60.

Course: glucose gel 15 g by mouth then juice and crackers. Symptoms resolved within 15 minutes. Repeat POC glucose 118. HbA1c 7.2%. Observed through lunch, glucose stable.

Impression: symptomatic severe hypoglycemia, insulin-treated diabetes.
Disposition: home with daughter. Eat before walking; carry fast sugar. Follow up with PCP this week to review insulin.

documents.title: Patient report: ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Went to the ED Saturday - got dizzy, heart pounding, sweaty while walking before breakfast-ish; sugar was 60 there. Treated with glucose, sent home. Feels fine now. Had a few similar spells the past 2 weeks he hadn't checked. Sugars since: 98-160. Advised to eat before walks and check before heading out. Visit booked 5/17. ED record requested.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypoglycemia without coma

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after the 5/7 ED visit for a low sugar (60) while walking. ED record not yet here; history from him and his meter. Since then he eats toast before his walk and checks first. No further spells. Meter download: fasting 100-165, one 72 late morning on a dialysis day.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Comfortable. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
Hypoglycemia episode, resolved. Reviewed the warning signs and treatment with sugar tabs or juice; he will keep a source in his jacket. Insulin doses unchanged.
T2DM - A1c 7.2 in the ED per his discharge paper.
RTC August.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination

documents.body: Diabetic eye exam 6/14/2022, dilated. No diabetic retinopathy. No macular edema. Cataracts mild. Recall 1 year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
No more low spells. ED note from May arrived in June - reviewed; it lists metformin, which he has never taken here (not appropriate on dialysis); confirmed with him he takes no metformin. Dialysis three days a week. Rides less reliable this summer - county service cut routes; his daughter fills in.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Lungs clear, no edema. Feet: no lesions, sensation intact.

T2DM - A1c, lipids, LFTs, CBC today. Same insulin.
Transportation - gave him the Medicaid ride benefit number as a backup.
RTC fall, flu and COVID booster at nurse visit.

conditions.label: Acute pulmonary edema
conditions.note: volume overload after two missed dialysis sessions

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Enlarged cardiac silhouette. Bilateral perihilar alveolar opacities. No pneumothorax. Costophrenic angles partly obscured.
reports.conclusion: Cardiomegaly with bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates, consistent with pulmonary edema.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 106. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ST elevation.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED record, date of service 11/09/2022.

CC: can't catch his breath.
HPI: 71 y/o man, ESRD on HD, T2DM, HTN, anemia of CKD, history of treated TB and a hypoglycemic episode this spring. Breathing has worsened over two days; now winded crossing a room and has spent the last two nights sitting up in a recliner because lying flat is impossible. Weight up about 5 lb and passing less urine this week. Missed his last two dialysis sessions (Friday and Monday) - his ride fell through both times.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5, sevelamer 800 with meals, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40.
Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: T 36.8, BP 172/94, HR 106, RR 28, SpO2 86% RA.
Exam: uncomfortable, dyspneic, speaking in short phrases. JVD to 10 cm above the sternal angle. Diffuse crackles both lungs. S3 present. Moderate pitting edema both legs. L AVF with thrill.
ABG on room air: hypoxemia with a widened A-a gradient.
CXR: enlarged cardiac silhouette, bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates. ECG: sinus tachycardia, LVH.

Course: nasal cannula 4 L, SpO2 95%. Furosemide IV given. Nephrology called; emergent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration arranged.
Impression: acute pulmonary edema from volume overload, missed hemodialysis.
Disposition: admitted to medicine for urgent dialysis.

documents.title: Dialysis unit call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Dialysis unit nurse called. Mr. Washington was admitted 11/9 with fluid on the lungs after missing two treatments (no ride). Had urgent dialysis in the hospital with 3.5 L removed, oxygen weaned, discharged 11/11. Back on his usual MWF schedule today, at his target weight, breathing comfortably. Unit social worker setting up a standing ride with a backup. Hospital discharge summary not sent to us - requested from the hospital. Post-hospital visit booked 11/21.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after admission 11/9-11/11 for pulmonary edema after two missed dialysis sessions. Discharge summary still not received despite request; ED record not yet in. History from patient, daughter and the dialysis unit's call.
Breathing back to normal, sleeping flat on one pillow. No chest pain. Dialysis on schedule since 11/14; unit says he's at target weight. Med list unchanged; no new prescriptions from the hospital.
Rides: unit social worker set a standing ride plus his daughter as backup. He knows that missing even one session is dangerous - if no ride, call the unit and us the same morning.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. No JVD. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, no gallop today. No leg edema. AVF thrill.

A/P
Acute pulmonary edema from missed dialysis - resolved.
ESRD on HD - per nephrology.
Med reconciliation done.
RTC February.

documents.title: Ride check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Follow-up call after November's missed sessions. Standing ride to dialysis has worked every treatment since. He has the unit's number and ours for any ride failure.

AWV.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2015 normal, due 2025. LDCT March Lung-RADS 2. Shingrix, pneumococcal, Tdap done. Flu/COVID this fall; RSV vaccine discussed - he'd like it in the fall too.
A1c today.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED - physician note, 11/23/2023 (Thanksgiving).

CC: fever and shaking chills.
HPI: 72 y/o man on maintenance HD with prior TB (treated) and pulmonary edema last year. Fever and chills for two days; they began a few hours after his Tuesday treatment (holiday-week schedule at his unit). No cough, no dysuria, nothing localizing.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5, sevelamer 800 with meals, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.7 C (101.7 F), BP 95/60, HR 102, RR 18.
Exam: ill-appearing but alert. Left arm AV fistula healed, no redness, warmth or tenderness over the access; thrill present. Lungs clear. No murmur appreciated. Abdomen soft.
Labs: WBC 12.0 (4.5-11.0), Hgb 10.2, platelets 220, BUN 45, creatinine 5.6 (baseline 5.2). Blood cultures x2 drawn before antibiotics.

Course: IV fluid bolus with care given ESRD; BP improved. Vancomycin 1 g IV.
Impression: sepsis, suspected dialysis access-related bacteremia.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

conditions.label: Sepsis due to Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size. LVEF 55-60%. Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. No valvular vegetations seen. No significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation. Normal right ventricular size and function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No echocardiographic evidence of endocarditis. Preserved LV function; mild concentric LVH.

medications.sig: 2 g IV after each hemodialysis through 12/22/2023

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - community hospital medicine service. Admitted 11/23/2023, discharged 11/28/2023. (Sent on request.)

Principal diagnosis: sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, related to vascular access.
Other: ESRD on HD via L AVF; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; anemia of CKD; history of treated pulmonary TB.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED febrile and hypotensive. Blood cultures from 11/23 grew MSSA in 2 of 2 sets. Fistula examined daily - no erythema, fluctuance or tenderness; vascular surgery reviewed, no drainable collection, source presumed cannulation-related. Vancomycin changed to cefazolin once susceptibilities returned. Repeat cultures 11/25 no growth. TTE 11/24: normal LV size, EF 55-60%, mild concentric LVH, no vegetations. Fever resolved by hospital day 2; BP normal off fluids. Dialysis continued on schedule in hospital.

Discharge medications: cefazolin 2 g IV after each dialysis through 12/22/2023 (given at the dialysis unit). Home medications unchanged: glargine 24 units qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; dialysis unit to monitor.

documents.title: Daughter call: hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called: her father has been in the hospital since Thanksgiving with a blood infection from his dialysis access. Fever gone, expected home tomorrow on IV antibiotics at dialysis. She'll bring him in after discharge. Booked post-hospital visit 12/6. Records requested from the hospital.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter after admission 11/23-11/28 for sepsis from a staph bloodstream infection tied to his dialysis access. ED record arrived 12/4; discharge summary not yet. Per patient and the discharge paperwork he brought: MSSA, switched to cefazolin, which the dialysis unit gives after each treatment until 12/22. Heart ultrasound in hospital was ok. No fevers since he left, appetite returning, tired.

Exam: afebrile, BP R arm as charted. Alert. L AVF: no redness, warmth or tenderness, good thrill. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
MSSA access-related bacteremia with sepsis - on cefazolin at HD through 12/22. Call for any fever or change at the fistula.
Med reconciliation: no other changes.
RTC February.

documents.title: Antibiotics at dialysis
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Daughter writing - Dad asked me to tell you the dialysis nurses say he has 2 more antibiotic treatments, last one Friday the 22nd. No fever. Arm looks fine.

documents.title: Re: Antibiotics at dialysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update - glad he's doing well. Call us right away for any fever, chills or redness around the fistula. We'll see him in February.
